title: A preadditive category with finite products, kernels and cokernels in which coimage equals image is abelian
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive category (hom-sets abelian groups, composition bilinear) which has finite products, kernels and cokernels. For a morphism $f:A\to B$ let $\operatorname{Coim}f=\operatorname{Coker}(\operatorname{Ker}f\to A)$ and $\operatorname{Im}f=\operatorname{Ker}(B\to\operatorname{Coker}f)$, and let $\theta_f:\operatorname{Coim}f\to\operatorname{Im}f$ be the canonical morphism (the unique one whose composite with $A\to\operatorname{Coim}f$ and $\operatorname{Im}f\to B$ is $f$). If $\theta_f$ is an isomorphism for every morphism $f$ of $\mathcal C$, then $\mathcal C$ is an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]: it has a zero object and finite biproducts, and every monomorphism is a kernel and every epimorphism is a cokernel.

source.place: Homology, Definition 0109 (definition-abelian-category, line 608): Stacks defines an abelian category as an additive category with kernels and cokernels in which Coim -> Im is an isomorphism; this node is the passage from that definition to the definition of def-sp-abelian, as used at the end of the proof of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X
